newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico manufacturing employment up 3.8 pct in July.
newsitem.headline: Mexico manufacturing employment up 3.8 pct in July.

text.p: Employment in Mexico's manufacturing sector rose 3.8 percent in July over the same month last year, marking the fourth straight month of increases, the government statistics institute INEGEI said.
"In July of this year the occupied personnel in the manufacturing industry increased 3.8 percent compared to the same month of the previous year," INEGI said in a news release.
The INEGI report also said man-hours in the manufacturing industry increased by 7.7 percent during the same period.
Seven of nine divisions in the country's manufacturing sector showed increases in employment in July 1996 over July 1995.

The employment growth was seen in: textiles, clothing and leather goods, 10.8 percent; metal products, machinery and equipment, 9.1 percent; basic metals, 8.3 percent; wood and wood products, 3.8 percent; chemicals, petroleum derivatives and plastics, 2.5 percent; food, beverages and tobacco, 0.5 percent; and "other industrial manufacturing", 9.7 percent
In contrast, employment fell by 1.5 percent in non-metalic mining and fell by 1.1 percent in paper, paper products, printing and publishing in July of this year compared to the same month last year.
